historical_declarations.text: 押しやすさ: 平行移動のため面のどこを押しても同じ力。この読み方はオーナー確認待ちの解釈。実機の押下感・クリック感は未試験。

Press force: the leaves add 0.08-0.53 N to the fitted switch operating force at the click (registered maxima up to 1.47 N; minima not published) and up to 0.72 N at the stop (thin/thick leaf limits and the preload range).

Switch profiles (insert rule and stop from datasheets): zippy_df_pin: pass (past OP at the stop 0.08-0.50 mm vs guaranteed OT 0.20: UNKNOWN (beyond the guaranteed minimum; no rating published); pin may bottom first: yes (tolerance corner: the switch takes the force there; bottoming rating UNKNOWN)); omron_d2f_pin: pass (past OP at the stop 0.08-0.50 mm vs guaranteed OT 0.25: UNKNOWN (beyond the guaranteed minimum; no rating published); pin may bottom first: yes (tolerance corner: the switch takes the force there; bottoming rating UNKNOWN)); huano_mouse_generic: unverified (missing operating_position, movement_differential, plunger_width, overtravel); kailh_gm20: unverified (missing operating_position, movement_differential, body_height, plunger_width, body_length, body_width, overtravel).
Leaves: beam theory only (guided small deflection, rigid root, typical datasheet values, ASSUMED stress concentration and Poisson ratio); creep and fatigue UNKNOWN; creep would lower the preload.

Overtravel past OP at the stop can exceed the guaranteed minimum for some inserts; no maker publishes a rating beyond it (UNKNOWN). In a tolerance corner the pin may bottom before the stop; bottoming rating UNKNOWN.

Insert retention: the outward load is the switch pin force (up to 1.47 N at the stop; the thumb force goes into the stop). Band retention in printed ABS is UNKNOWN: first-article test = pull-out force >= 3 N with a gram gauge before the insert rule is used.
Rest lip preload, pin retention and the carrier placement tolerance are ASSUMED, not measured; first article: feeler-gauge the face-to-skin step at both ends and the stop travel.
PCB plane is ASSUMED; the real board and shell were not measured. OP1-supplied screws are not used by this carrier.
Wall checks are sampled minima of the stated parts, not a proof of minimum wall or of strength. Placement corners are rigid corners only.

resolution_boundary.next_step: A later resolution proposal must identify declaration IDs and bind new evidence; this view is not a completed resolution ledger.
resolution_boundary.statement: Measurements are observations, not automatic resolutions of natural-language declarations. Geometry pass does not prove physical performance, manufacturing, missing inputs or every clause of a compound declaration.

open_blockers.claim: The click-before-stop stack (stack_v18) passes only because its stop-travel range (0.5 +/- 0.1) leaves out the carrier yaw that the design itself declares (+/-0.18 deg). The parallel leaves carry the block yaw to the face. The lip then rests on its most outward end, and the stop tab (x 12-16.9) sits near the far end. When I apply the declared yaw, the travel from rest to the stop drops to 0.414 mm. With the declared -0.1 face error, the worst travel is 0.314 mm. The insert rule allows the tip to rest up to 0.32 mm above OP, so the switch can meet the hard stop before it clicks. F5 promises a stop 'after the worst-case click', and the check reports pass, so the pass is false under the design's own declared tolerances. A far-end press (the declared 0.32 deg yaw at 3 N) makes it worse. The tab corner reaches the jaw before the tip has moved its share, and no check sees this because the rotation checks leave out stop_jaw and stop_post.
evidence: Own probe (rigid rotation of button+insert and rest_lip about (-27.65,15.35) Z by the declared carrier-placement angle, bisection on contact): rot 0 -> rest offset -0.300, stop offset -0.800, travel 0.500; rot +0.18247 deg -> travel 0.5035; rot -0.18247 deg -> rest -0.2441, stop -0.6581, travel 0.414 mm.
stack_v18: t_lo = stop_travel 0.5 - 0.1 = 0.4; rest_above_op upper = md + 2s = 0.12 + 0.2 = 0.32 (zippy/omron md 0.12) -> past_op low 0.08 reported. With the yaw: 0.414 - 0.1 - 0.32 = -0.006 mm.
carrier_tolerance_v18 uses the yaw only for the preload range (face_y_variation), never in stack_v18's travel range.

Own probe, far-end yaw -0.3249 deg about (-9,15.3) (the declared far-end press case): button to stop_jaw 0.153 mm already at the -0.5 pose and overlapping (0.61 mm3) at -0.75, i.e. the tab corner meets the jaw about 0.15 mm early; at x=2 (insert) the same yaw adds only ~0.06 mm, so tip travel at the stop drops by ~0.085 mm.
rotation_checks edge/far-end/corner obstacles = ['shell','pcb_slab'] only; stop_jaw and stop_post are not obstacles.
design_basis: 'the worst-case click is 0.32 mm after rest' and F5 'stops the far-end tab 0.5 +/- 0.1 mm after rest (after the worst-case click)'.
open_blockers.proposed_change: Add the carrier-placement yaw (both signs) and the press-induced yaw to stack_v18's travel range. Measure it with the rest contact (lip) and the stop contact (tab on jaw) as here, not from the nominal 0.5 mm. Then restore a positive margin. Options: a longer nominal stop travel; putting the stop tab near the insert x so that yaw moves both by the same amount; or a smaller insert step. Also state that the insert rule has to be checked by an actual click at the stop, at a far-end press as well as a centre press.
open_blockers.required_test: Re-run stack_v18 with t_lo derived from the measured rest/stop contacts at both yaw signs plus the print error, plus a far-end-press translation-with-yaw sweep that includes stop_jaw and stop_post as obstacles and reports the tip travel past the rest at tab contact; require tip travel at stop >= rest_above_op_max + margin for every insert the rule can pick.

open_blockers.claim: stack_v18 reports "pass" for zippy_df_pin and omron_d2f_pin. By its own verdict_scope this means "the switch operates before the hard stop for every insert the rule can choose". The proof uses only stop travel 0.5-0.1 = 0.4 mm against the worst-case click of 0.32 mm (MD 0.12 + 2 x 0.1 step), a margin of 0.08 mm. It assumes "rest and stop are on the shell and do not move with it". That holds for translation but not for rotation. The rest lip (27.2 mm long) and the far-end stop tab (x up to 16.9) are both on the button. The declared carrier rotation of +/-0.182 deg makes the face seat on one lip end and leaves the far end 0.087 mm deeper, which shortens the stop travel. The recipe's own far-end press yaw of 0.325 deg about the leaf tip brings the far-end tab to the jaw before the plunger at x=2 has travelled the full stop distance. With the declared tolerances and load case, the plunger travel at the stop is 0.23-0.31 mm, below the 0.32 mm worst-case click. A far-end press with an insert at the upper end of the rule can then hit the hard stop without operating the switch, so the "pass" is false.
evidence: scripts/side_button_leaf_recipe.py stack_v18: past_op = (t_lo - rest_above_op[1], ...) with t_lo = 0.4 and rest_above_op = (0.1, 0.32); verdict pass when past_op[0] > 0 (0.08). Neither carrier rotation nor guide yaw enters the stack.
carrier_tolerance_v18: rotation 0.18247 deg about (-27.65, 15.35); design_basis says "rest and stop are on the shell and do not move with it".

twist_v18: yaw_deg 0.3249 at 3 N on a 23 mm lever (k_yaw 12168 Nmm/rad, thin limit). The rotation_checks use axis (-9, 15.3), so the tab at x 16.9 moves 25.9 x 0.00567 = 0.147 mm and the plunger at x 2 moves 0.062 mm.

Own probe (CadQuery on the exported button, rest_lip, shell and stop_jaw STEP; rest found by bisection on lip-shell overlap, then translation to the first button-jaw overlap): plunger travel from rest to the stop = 0.500 mm at nominal, 0.504 mm at carrier +0.182 deg, 0.414 mm at -0.182 deg.

Own probe with the far-end yaw -0.3249 deg (far end inward) added at rest: plunger travel at the stop = 0.415 mm (carrier nominal) and 0.330 mm (carrier -0.182 deg). With yaw -0.223 deg (the force when the tab meets the jaw, about 2 N = leaves 0.59 N + switch 1.47 N): 0.356 / 0.271 mm.
Applying the declared stop tolerance of -0.1 mm: 0.315 mm (yaw only), 0.314 mm (carrier rotation only), 0.230 mm (both), all below rest_above_op max 0.32 mm.

Insert rule (design_basis) is referenced to release only ("longest insert with which the switch still releases ... then the next shorter one"), so nothing at fitting checks or restores the click before the stop.
open_blockers.proposed_change: Put the stop and the rest datum where rotation cannot shorten the plunger travel. One way is two stop tabs, one each side of the plunger (near end and far end), or one stop on the plunger axis (x of about 2). Alternatively, make the stop click-referenced: a jaw thickness series in 0.05 mm steps chosen at fitting so that the click occurs at least 0.1 mm before the stop. Add the carrier rotation and the far-end and corner yaw terms to stack_v18 (travel at the plunger, not at the tab), and let the verdict fail when the minimum is at or below the worst-case click.
open_blockers.required_test: Extend stack_v18 to compute plunger travel at the stop under carrier-placement corners combined with +/- yaw at the declared press force, and require past_op_min > 0 with a stated margin. Add a CAD motion check that applies the yaw pose about the leaf-tip axis plus a translation and measures plunger travel at first button-jaw contact. Physical first article: with the longest insert the rule allows, press at the far end of the face with a 3 N gauge and confirm the click occurs before the stop on 3 assemblies.
